fields.summary: User can reset their password via an emailed link
fields.description:
As a registered user I want to reset my password through a link sent to my email so that I can regain access when I forget it.

Project Key: SMOKE
Issue ID (numeric): 10001

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form sends an email with a single-use password-reset link that is valid for 60 minutes.
2. Opening a reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent shows the message 'This reset link has expired' and a 'Request a new link' button.

attachments.reset-policy.md:
Password reset policy
- A reset link stays valid for 60 minutes.
- At most 3 reset requests per account per hour.

test_cases.name: Verify password reset with valid single-use link within 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify that submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form sends a single-use reset link valid within 60 minutes, which successfully resets the password and cannot be reused.
test_cases.precondition:
Register a user account for registered.user@example.com through the sign-up form
Access to the email inbox for 'registered.user@example.com' is available.
The application is accessible.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] weak step and imprecise expected result (AC-1): Step S3 represents the weakest step in the test case: its expected result vaguely states that 'A confirmation message indicating that the password has been reset successfully and that the user can now log in with the new password is displayed', which asserts that the user can now log in without actually verifying that the updated credentials work in the system, and fails to specify the concrete confirmation message or subsequent UI state. As a result, a tester could execute the verification inconsistently or fail to detect defects where the backend did not actually update the password.
    Suggested fix: Update step S3 to make its expected result more precise by specifying the concrete confirmation message and UI state transition (e.g., 'A confirmation message stating that the password has been successfully reset is displayed, and the user is redirected to the login page') to ensure unambiguous verification of the reset action.
  • [HIGH] weak step and missing expected result (AC-1): Step 1 is the weakest step of the test case because it conflates submitting the 'Forgot password' form with opening the reset email ('Request a password-reset link for registered.user@example.com and open the reset email') and completely omits verifying the web application's response upon form submission. AC-1 specifies submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form. Without explicitly verifying the immediate feedback on the web page (such as a confirmation notice indicating that a reset email has been sent), a tester could execute the verification inconsistently or fail to detect defects on the Forgot Password confirmation screen before navigating to the email client.
    Suggested fix: Modify Step 1 to explicitly describe the submission actions on the 'Forgot password' form (entering the registered email address and clicking the submit button) and verify the expected UI response (displaying a confirmation message confirming that the reset email has been dispatched) prior to opening the received email.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

test_cases.name: Verify expiration of password reset link after 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify that opening a password reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent displays an expiration message and a 'Request a new link' button that redirects back to the 'Forgot password' page.
test_cases.precondition:
A user account with email 'user@example.com' is registered in the system.
Access to the email inbox for 'user@example.com' is available.
A password-reset email with a reset link has already been sent to 'user@example.com'.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result (AC-2): Step 2 is the weakest step of the test case because its expected result ('The user is redirected to the \'Forgot password\' page, displaying the email address input field and the submit button ready for entering an email address.') lacks precision and deviates from the recorded procedure [proc-submit-forgot-password] 'Submit the email address on the \'Forgot password\' form'. The expected result refers vaguely to 'the submit button ready for entering an email address', conflating the input field with the button and omitting the button's exact label. According to [proc-submit-forgot-password], the button on the 'Forgot password' page is labeled 'Send reset link'. As a consequence, testers may verify the destination page inconsistently or fail to notice an incorrectly labeled submit button.
    Suggested fix: Modify the expected result of Step 2 to: 'The user is redirected to the \'Forgot password\' page, displaying an empty email address input field and the \'Send reset link\' button.'
  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result (AC-2): Step 1 is the weakest step of the test case because while its expected result checks for the message 'This reset link has expired' and the 'Request a new link' button, it fails to verify that the password reset form and input fields (new password and confirm password) are absent or inaccessible. AC-2 requires link expiration after 60 minutes; omitting the verification that the reset form cannot be accessed or submitted allows a critical defect—where the form remains functional despite the expiration notice—to be overlooked by testers.
    Suggested fix: Update the expected result of Step 1 to explicitly confirm that the password reset form and its input fields are not displayed or accessible, in addition to verifying the presence of the message 'This reset link has expired' and the 'Request a new link' button.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.
